verdicts.note: Attacked on strength, since the ballot title and the statement for call it a 'restore' of a rate the 1% limit eroded (S1, S4). It does not hold up as a renewal. The rate goes from $0.228924 to $0.35 per $1,000, about 53% higher (S1, S3). That is about $14 million more districtwide in 2027 (S4, S5), through a levy lid lift under RCW 84.55.050 (S3), which the taxes pole_b names as cap lifts. Strength 2 matches Thurston's mapping of the same measure. S1, S4 and S5 each support the cited figures. No spending mapping was added: Mittge's 'increase it modestly but meaningfully with more hours' (S5) is the only expansion language, and the stated purpose is restoring service cut in 2026 (S1, S5). That is too thin for +1 at medium. No social or parental-rights mapping: the dossier finds nothing on collections or access policy.

what_it_does matches S1 (from $0.22 to $0.35 for 2027 and 2028; the 2028 amount is the base) and S1/S7 (96% of revenue). It matches S4 and S5 on restored hours, staffing and collections, and S6 on all five counties voting. cost_line matches S1/S3 ($0.228924; $40.44 on $334,000) and S4/S5 ($46 on the $357,400 Lewis median; about $14 million in 2027). pro_summary paraphrases the unsigned statement for, quotes 'a long overdue cost-of-living raise' accurately, and correctly says two of the four former trustees are from Lewis County (Fund, Zylstra; S7). con_summary paraphrases the unsigned statement against accurately and attributes the 'schools or public safety' question to Commissioner Swope as S5 reports it. No author is given to the guide statements, which matches the dossier.

Attacked toward 2: the tax expires June 30, 2027 if the measure fails (S1, S2), so a YES vote is the only way the 0.2% sales tax continues. The NO alternative is no TBD sales tax at all. But the measure renews an existing voter-approved tax at its current rate (S1, S3, S6), below the 0.3% state law allows (S5). Other packages treat renewals and replacements at the current rate as the renewal tier (1): Spokane's replacement school levies, Benton's Ki-Be replacement levy, Thurston's fire renewals. +1 is consistent with them. Attacked toward 0 and rejected: keeping a tax that would otherwise end is still a vote for continued revenue. The citations hold: S1 and S2 (renewal, expiry) and S6 (same rate, 2 cents on $10). No spending mapping: the purpose is maintaining streets and matching grants for named projects (S1, S4).

what_it_does matches S1/S2 (ten years, July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2037; uses limited to transportation; expiry if it fails) and S4 (local grant match). cost_line matches S1/S6 (0.2%, 20 cents per $100, current rate) and S1/S4 ($11.2 million since 2017). pro_summary: 'not a new tax' quotes S1. The $12.9 million in matched grants comes from the city via S4, not from the statement for (S1 says only that the tax provides the local match 'often required'). The sentence reads as if the statement says so, a small attribution looseness that is not worth a correction. The named projects match S1, S4 and S6. con_summary matches S1 and S8 (no statement against, no committee) and S3 (45.10% voted no in 2017).

Attacked on strength. S1 and S2 both say the rate for the remaining district would otherwise be about $0.99 to $1.00 after the Chehalis annexation, so measured against the no-vote alternative the increase is about 16% ($0.99 to $1.15), not the 'roughly half' the basis says, which compares against the pre-annexation $0.73-$0.79. Even so, it is a levy lid lift that resets the base upward (S1), the rubric's pole_b example. It raises the rate well above both the current rate and the no-vote rate, and it is not a renewal of an expiring levy. That is consistent with strength 2 for Whatcom Fire District 1 (about 32%) and Spokane Fire Districts 3 and 9. Direction and strength are upheld, but the basis wording overstates the effective increase. S1 and S2 support the rate figures. No spending mapping: the district frames it as maintaining current staffing, response times and apparatus after lost revenue (S1, S2).

what_it_does matches S1 ($1.15 for 2027 collection; listed uses; base for later limits), S3 (rural Chehalis and Adna) and S2/S5 ($193,000 a year lost to the 2026 Chehalis annexation; effective June 2026 per S5). cost_line gives both current-rate figures and the $0.99 post-annexation rate (S1, S2), but '$126 more a year on a $300,000 property' is computed from $0.73 (S2). Against the $0.99 no-vote rate the difference is about $48. A reader could take $126 as the measure's marginal cost. Suggested cost_line ending: 'The district's flyer puts the difference at $126 a year on a $300,000 property measured from $0.73; against the $0.99 rate expected without the measure it is about $48.' pro_summary matches S2 (no lid lift on the fire levy in 20+ years, staffing and response times, aging apparatus, annexation) and S1 (no statement for filed). It says 'call volume has grown'; S2 gives 1,034 responses in 2025 and cites keeping up with call volume as a failure risk, and S1 cites 'rising demands', so this is supported. con_summary matches S1 and S7.
